'''Amari Bailey''' (born February 17, 2004) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]] of the [[Pac-12 Conference]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class.

==Early life and high school career==
Born in [[New Orleans]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Amari Bailey|publisher=UCLA Athletics|url=https://uclabruins.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/amari-bailey/11347|access-date=November 13, 2022}}</ref> Bailey grew up in [[Chicago]], and was raised by a single mother.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Yapkowitz |first1=David |title=Amari Bailey: “I want to be the best player I can be in high school” |url=https://www.marsreel.com/amari-bailey-i-want-to-be-the-best-player-i-can-be-in-high-school/ |website=Mars Reel |access-date=July 17, 2021 |date=May 20, 2019}}</ref><ref name=spears_04082022>{{cite news|first=Marc. J.|last=Spears|title=Top prospect Amari Bailey is changing perceptions on his way to UCLA, the NBA|date=April 8, 2022|work=Andscape|url=https://andscape.com/features/top-prospect-amari-bailey-is-changing-perceptions-on-his-way-to-ucla-the-nba/|access-date=May 3, 2022}}</ref> He and his mother were featured in ''Bringing Up Ballers'', a [[Lifetime (TV network)|Lifetime]] reality show that follows Chicago-area entrepreneur mothers of basketball players.<ref name=spears_04082022/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Swartz |first1=Tracy |title=New Lifetime series to feature young Chicago basketball standouts |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/ct-bringing-up-ballers-lifetime-chicago-20170201-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=July 17, 2021 |date=February 1, 2017}}</ref> He moved to the Los Angeles area to play for [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, Los Angeles|Chatsworth]].<ref name=spears_04082022/><ref name=sondheimer_03092019/> As a [[freshman (education)|freshman]], Bailey helped his team win the [[California Interscholastic Federation]] Open Division state title.<ref name=sondheimer_03092019>{{cite web |last1=Sondheimer |first1=Eric |title=Sierra Canyon claims second Open Division state title with win over Sheldon |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/highschool/la-sp-sierra-canyon-sheldon-20190309-story.html |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=July 17, 2021 |date=March 9, 2019}}</ref> He had nine points, 2021}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Bailey was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. At age 13, while in eighth grade, he committed to playing college basketball for [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]], but he decommitted before starting high school.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fielding |first1=Lisa |title=Eighth Grade Chicago Basketball Star Commits To DePaul |url=https://chicago.cbslocal.com/2017/08/14/basketball-commitment-depaul-amari-bailey/ |website=[[WBBM-TV]] |access-date=July 17, 2021 |date=August 14, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Steeno |first1=Paul |title=Eighth grader no longer committed to DePaul |url=https://depauliaonline.com/33919/sports/eighth-grader-no-longer-committed-to-depaul/ |website=[[The DePaulia]] |access-date=July 17, 2021 |date=March 16, 2018}}</ref> He later committed to [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] as a high school freshman, before decommitting again eight months later when their coach, [[Steve Alford]], was fired.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Newman |first1=Logan |title=Report: Sierra Canyon 2022 star Amari Bailey decommits from UCLA |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/2022-amari-bailey-decommits-from-ucla |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=July 17, 2021 |date=July 1, 2019}}</ref><ref name=bolch_02172021>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Highly coveted prospect Amari Bailey returns ‘home’ in picking UCLA|date=February 17, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-02-17/highly-coveted-prospect-amari-bailey-ucla|access-date=May 10, 2022}}</ref> On February 17, 2021, Bailey recommitted to UCLA and their new coach, [[Mick Cronin (basketball)|Mick Cronin]].<ref name=bolch_02172021/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Amari Bailey, a highly regarded high school junior guard, commits to UCLA basketball a second time |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30920547/amari-bailey-highly-regarded-high-school-junior-guard-commits-ucla-second |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 17, 2021 |date=February 17, 2021}}</ref> Bailey was seen as the number one player by every recruiting service entering the summer off his senior season before suffering an injury which resulted in Bailey to miss playing in the [[AAU Men's Basketball All-Americans|AAU]] circuit and early parts off Sierra Canyon season . <ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Bailey - Men's Basketball |url=https://uclabruins.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/amari-bailey/11347 |access-date=2023-04-12 |website=UCLA |language=en}}</ref>

[[247Sports]] ranked Bailey as the third-best [[combo guard]] in his high school class.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=High-flying Amari Bailey should make an instant impact for UCLA with skills and savvy|date=October 31, 2022|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-10-31/amari-bailey-ucla-basketball-impact-freshman|access-date=November 3, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
In his college debut, Bailey scored 10 points against [[Sacramento State Hornets men's basketball|Sacramento State]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA’s Amari Bailey may be goofy off the court, but freshman courts serious accolades|date=February 22, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-02-22/ucla-bruins-amari-bailey-pac-12-freshman|access-date=February 14, 2023}}</ref> He began the [[2022–23 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2022–23 season]] winning the [[Pac-12 Conference]]'s freshman of the week award twice.<ref name=fattal_01112023>{{cite web|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=No. 7 UCLA’s 11-game win streak on the line against Utah|date=January 11, 2023|work=The Orange County Register|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2023/01/11/no-7-uclas-11-game-win-streak-on-the-line-against-utah/|access-date=January 15, 2023}}</ref> He was injured against [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] when the Wildcats' [[Oscar Tshiebwe]] stepped on his left foot.  Bailey aggravated the injury the following game against [[UC Davis Aggies men's basketball|UC Davis]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA’s Amari Bailey appears unlikely to play against Arizona State with lingering foot issue|date=January 17, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-01-17/ucla-basketball-amari-bailey-foot-injury-mick-cronin-arizona-state|access-date=January 20, 2023}}</ref> From December 30, 2022, against [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]], until January 26, 2023, he was sidelined for seven games due to discomfort in his foot.<ref name=fattal_01112023/><ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Mick Cronin gets his comeback as UCLA fends off upset-minded Washington State|date=December 30, 2022|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-12-30/ucla-basketball-washington-state-comeback-win-recap|access-date=January 15, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-01-25/amari-bailey-return-ucla-usc-basketball|title= Amari Bailey available to return for No. 8 UCLA’s showdown with USC |work=LA Times|date=January 25, 2023|first=Ben|last=Bolch}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=No. 8 UCLA sees repeat mistakes in 2nd straight Pac-12 loss|date=January 26, 2023|work=Orange County Register|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2023/01/26/no-8-ucla-sees-repeat-mistakes-in-2nd-straight-pac-12-loss/|access-date=February 5, 2023}}</ref> On February 9, Bailey scored 24 points in a win against [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=No. 7 UCLA shakes off slow start to put on a defensive show in win over Oregon State|date=February 9, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-02-09/ucla-vs-oregon-state-gamer-recap|access-date=February 24, 2023}}</ref> After UCLA's best defender, [[Jaylen Clark]], suffered a season-ending leg injury in the regular-season finale against [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA freshmen’s stingy defense could give Bruins a boost against Gonzaga|date=March 22, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-22/ucla-gonzaga-basketball-sweet-16-preview-ncaa-tournament|access-date=March 23, 2023}}</ref> Bailey assumed the task of defending the opposition's top perimeter player,<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Amari Bailey’s moment has arrived. How far will it take him and UCLA?|date=March 19, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-19/amari-bailey-ucla-basketball-ncaa-tournament|access-date=March 20, 2023}}</ref> and he also increased his scoring.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Jaylen Clark is out but still inspiring defense-minded UCLA in NCAA tournament|date=March 17, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-17/ucla-northwestern-second-round-ncaa-tournament-northwestern|access-date=March 20, 2023}}</ref> In the Bruins' opener in the [[2023 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|2023 Pac-12 tournament]], Bailey scored a career-high 26 points in a win over [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Amari Bailey bails out Jaylen Clark-depleted Bruins in comeback over Colorado|date=March 9, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-03-09/amari-bailey-ucla-colorado-pac-12-tournament-recap|access-date=March 10, 2023}}</ref> He had 19 points and seven rebounds in the finals, which UCLA lost 61–59 to Arizona.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=No. 2 seed UCLA opens NCAA Tournament vs. UNC Asheville|date=March 12, 2023|work=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/03/12/no-2-seed-ucla-opens-ncaa-tournament-vs-unc-asheville/|access-date=March 12, 2023}}</ref> He helped the Bruins advance to the Sweet 16 of the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023 NCAA tournament]], averaging 15.5 points and 6.0 assists while converting 49.5% of his [[field goal (basketball)|field goals]] and 38.9% of his [[three-point field goal|three-pointers]]. In the six games after Clark's injury, Bailey averaged 17.3 points and shot 56.1%. He ended the season with averages of 11.2 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.2 assists in 30 games.<ref name=bolch_04132023/> He was named to the Pac-12 All-Freshman Team.<ref>{{cite press release|title=2022-23 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference honors and Annual Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva|date=March 7, 2023|publisher=Pac-12 Conference|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2023/03/07/2022-23-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-and-annual-performance|access-date=March 7, 2023}}</ref> After the season, he [[NBA draft declaration|declared]] for the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref name=bolch_04132023>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=After stellar freshman season, UCLA’s Amari Bailey declares for the NBA draft|date=April 13, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2023-04-13/ucla-amari-bailey-declares-for-nba-draft|access-date=May 8, 2023}}</ref>

==National team career==
Bailey represented the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in Brazil. He averaged 13.2 points, 4.2 rebounds and three assists per game, helping his team win the gold medal.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fisher |first1=Chris |title=Kentucky, Kansas recruiting top-5 junior the hardest |url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Article/Kentucky-basketball-recruiting-Amari-Bailey-151343787/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=July 17, 2021 |date=September 11, 2020}}</ref>
